newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end up, secondaries pull back.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end up, secondaries pull back.

text.p: Malaysian blue chips extended Friday's gains at the close on renewed institutional interest, but Second Board stocks mostly retreated on profit-taking, dealers said.

They said gains continued to be led by second-liner main board stocks, which have been the target of speculative buying since the beginning of the year. "People are calling it the Chinese New Year rally. So you can expect another two weeks of play," said a dealer with a bank-backed brokerage.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks ended up 11.14 points or 0.91 percent to 1,235.69.
The Second Board index fell 7.24 points or 1.18 percent to 605.69.
Leading the blue chip rise was Malayan Banking which surged 1.00 ringgit to 27.00 on expectations of strong half year earnings. Tenaga Nasional, Sime Darby and Proton rose 10 cents each.

Telekom Malaysia recovered 10 cents to 20.40 ringgit after falling sharply last week on shifting of portfolios by fund managers, rumours of lower-than-forecast full-year earnings, worries about industry competition and alleged discrepancies in a tender award.
